why: MI-280 session-end duty, not a new unit. CLAUDE.md's 'End:' section requires a session to 'add one for anything you shipped that is not yet proven on the fleet', and MI-280 shipped eight landing/register instruments of which only TWO have been observed acting. One row, docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json only — Tier-1, no src/, no config/, no deploy/, no code at all. ONE ROW RATHER THAN EIGHT, deliberately: eight rows for one session's output is the desensitised-alarm shape the register itself warns about, and the register is what every session reads at start. The row carries EIGHT SEPARATE clears_when clauses instead, each naming its own cheap read, with an explicit instruction not to close the row because most of them cleared. THE OBSERVATION IS REAL AND IS NOT A CLAIM OF PROGRESS. U2's detector was read off its own workflow run logs on its own two pushes — `no_pr` then `armed`, a negative AND a positive state from a real push event — and U5's incumbent grading printed SPENT on the live merge slot against a branch git ls-remote could not find. The other six are deployed and unexercised and the row says so. TWO OF THEM CANNOT EXERCISE THEMSELVES AND THAT IS STRUCTURAL, stated rather than left as a gap someone will read as laziness: #11889 changes a workflow, and a workflow only runs from the version on main; #11891 would have to ARM to test its own route, and arming a LANDING_MACHINERY diff is precisely what R12 forbids. THE CHEAPEST CLAUSE IS LISTED FIRST ON PURPOSE — read sources.red_crons.state in a post-merge DUE.json — because a clears_when whose first step is expensive is one nobody starts. It also carries the warning that a stale artifact looks identical, so the reader must check WHICH commit wrote it. AND THE ROW RECORDS THE ONE MEASURED NUMBER THAT IS NOT YET ACTED ON: 181 of 184 automation/* branches on origin are genuinely stranded, full clone, graded against origin/main — which is why the U6 clause matters and why its probe having zero callers is filed separately.
hold_text: Must land after #11895 (MI-280 U6). This row's clears_when clause (5) cites BL-20260912-THE-STUCK-BRANCH-PROBE-IS-WIRED-TO-NOTHING-SO-181-STRANDED-AUTOMATION-BRANCHES-ARE-SEEN-BY-NOBODY, which is FILED ON #11895 and is not on main yet, so check_backlog_refs.py correctly refuses this branch: a register row saying 'tracked by BL-X' where BL-X does not exist reads as tracked while being tracked by nobody. I am NOT dropping the citation to get past the guard, and that is the whole decision here. The citation is the load-bearing half of clause (5): without it, a reader is told to observe the stuck-branch probe running on a cadence and is not told that the probe has ZERO callers, so the clause would read as a thing about to happen rather than a thing blocked on a carrier nobody has built. Dropping the id would make this PR pass and make the register worse. REMEDY IS ORDERING, NOT EDITING: merge #11895 first — it is Tier-1, landing: self, armed — and this becomes green with no change. If #11895 is rejected instead, the right fix is to re-file that backlog row on its own and re-point clause (5), NOT to delete the clause.
